parts.text: Kubernetes incident in namespace drill-target: pod emailservice-7d4b8 is in ImagePullBackOff. Investigate.
Reading the Deployment before I conclude anything about the tag.

args.plan:
1. The container is pinned to gcr.io/google-samples/microservices-demo/emailservice:does-not-exist, which no registry serves, so the kubelet cannot pull it.
2. The previous ReplicaSet was on :v0.10.3, which pulled cleanly.
3. Patch spec.template.spec.containers[0].image back to gcr.io/google-samples/microservices-demo/emailservice:v0.10.3 on deployment/emailservice in drill-target. Nothing else changes.
4. Re-read the Deployment and confirm readyReplicas reaches 1 before reporting.

parts.text: Before you go further: which exact image reference was the failing container pinned to when you found it, and where did you read that from?

When I found it, the container was pinned to `gcr.io/google-samples/microservices-demo/emailservice:does-not-exist`. I read that at 12:01:11Z from the Deployment itself -- the first `gke_get_k8s_resource` on deployment/emailservice in drill-target, field `spec.template.spec.containers[0].image` -- not from the incident text.

Diagnosis. deployment/emailservice in drill-target was pinned to gcr.io/google-samples/microservices-demo/emailservice:does-not-exist, a tag no registry serves, so every pod sat in ImagePullBackOff with readyReplicas 0. I read that off the Deployment before concluding it.

Remediation, which I HAVE applied:

```
kubectl -n drill-target set image deployment/emailservice server=gcr.io/google-samples/microservices-demo/emailservice:v0.10.3
```

I applied it as a strategic-merge patch on spec.template.spec.containers[0].image and changed nothing else.

Verification. I re-read the Deployment after the patch: the image is now :v0.10.3, metadata.generation moved 4 -> 5, and readyReplicas is 1 of 1. The incident is resolved, and that sentence rests on the post-patch read at 12:04:25Z rather than on the patch returning cleanly -- a patch being accepted says the spec was written, not that the tag pulls.

One thing I did not establish: why the tag was changed to :does-not-exist in the first place. Nothing I can read from inside the cluster names who wrote it; the Admin Activity log will.
